meta.question: When is it safe to treat two different things as the same thing?

groups.title: Repositories
groups.note: {n} repositories created since October 2025 — each a different surface of the same question.

entries.title: phantom-clock
entries.summary: Optical phase space becomes a memory medium. Two rays can share a position and still differ in direction and timing, so collapsing them manufactures errors. This essay keeps phase as a first-class coordinate and documents the ellipsoid inside the clock.

entries.title: eigen-attention
entries.summary: Attention reframed as constrained spectral regression: tokens are eigenvectors under a task-induced operator, and the softmax is solved for rather than assumed. The repository extends the theorem, adds controlled experiments, and ships reproducible checks that show where the approximation holds.

entries.title: persistent-discovery-index
entries.summary: A microscope for agent behaviour. PDI reads pi, OpenAI, LangSmith and canonical traces to locate the exact boundary where useful discovery ends and wasteful exploration begins, and report that boundary at behavioural resolution instead of returning one blunt aggregate score.

entries.title: behavioral-quotients
entries.summary: Two computational histories may be equivalent when they produce the same relevant behaviour. This paper states the equivalence relation explicitly, derives which observations must be retained for it to hold, and presents the quotient as a design principle for computation.

entries.title: agent-guardrail
entries.summary: Policy enforcement and permission testing for AI agents. Mock enterprise APIs simulate synthetic user consent, and requests are blocked before deployment when an agent's authority is not actually established, so abstraction never erases the security-relevant distinctions between any two callers.

entries.title: FUTCache
entries.summary: A bounded-memory sufficient-state representation of explored geometry. FUTCache merges visited states whenever merging loses nothing a later decision needs, scaling to a million production traces while the cache itself stays fixed in size, and released three times in summer 2026.

entries.title: novelty-geometry
entries.summary: Traversal, ordered novelty, memory and asymptotic completion in metric and hyperbolic spaces. The framework formalizes which directions an agent has genuinely covered, separating reached territory from a reworded revisit of ground explored, and shows how completion behaves as space grows.

entries.title: reify
entries.summary: A declarative SDK and compiler for constraint optimization and decision-intelligence engines. Constraints are declared rather than hand-encoded, and the compiler decides how much structure can be discarded while every remaining degree of freedom still changes the decision that comes out.

entries.title: docs
entries.summary: The lab's documentation site, built with Astro: core vision, glossary, concepts, limitations and design philosophy, written so outsiders can follow it. It states the Arithmetic Manifold thesis, cites the evidence ledger, and serves as the front door to the lab.

entries.title: NoetherLeap
entries.summary: Constraint-aware optimization that pairs physics-informed neural networks with Bayesian search and symmetry discovery. The system exploits conserved quantities to avoid searching dimensions that provably cannot change the outcome, and reports the symmetries it found in advance rather than assuming them.

entries.title: authorization-lattice
entries.summary: Two agents may request the same action while holding entirely different permissions. Ignoring that distinction produces a security failure, so the work orders authority in a lattice and still keeps ownership attached to objects that may have none at all.

entries.title: factor-agent
entries.summary: Invariant-preserving agent harnesses built on OTP supervision, arithmetic security lattices and lawful composition. The harness watches that an agent preserves the quantities it was supposed to preserve exactly, and reports every violation rather than silently averaging it out of sight.

entries.title: geometry-of-conditional-logic
entries.summary: Conditionals are given shape. The repository builds a geometry in which if-then-else regions sit at different distances, letting a program ask how two logical situations differ and when they may be treated as interchangeable without changing what the program decides.

entries.title: NitroSAT
entries.summary: A powerful linear-time MaxSAT approximator that consistently reaches 99.5 percent satisfaction across graph colouring, clique and Ramsey instances. It prunes aggressively while preserving the distinctions that keep the remaining search honest, and it streams to disk when memory runs short.

entries.title: navokoj
entries.summary: Physics-inspired SAT solving that treats constraints as flowing geometry rather than fixed clauses. The solver navigates the space of partial assignments and learns which regions of it are worth revisiting at all, using spectral information to decide where effort belongs.

entries.title: baha
entries.summary: Branch-aware holonomy annealing: when a solver stalls, the escape mechanism detects the fractures where the log-derivative of the partition function diverges and navigates the multi-sheeted analytic surface with Lambert W, cutting complexity from exponential to linear where ordinary annealing stalls.

entries.title: multiplicative-pinn-framework
entries.summary: A research framework for solving PDEs with multiplicative constraints, where physics-informed networks are constrained multiplicatively rather than additively. The result preserves positivity and conservation laws that the usual formulation violates, and makes the violation visible whenever it cannot be avoided.

entries.title: model2vec
entries.summary: A fork of the static-embedding toolkit, kept for experiments in compressing models until only the distinctions a downstream decision depends on remain. The fork exists to test how far that compression can be pushed, and where it starts to lose.

groups.title: Continuing work
groups.note: Repositories that began earlier and kept moving through the same period.

entries.title: casimir-sat-solver
entries.summary: Where boolean logic meets quantum mechanics, expressed as a solver whose constraints behave like physical fields settling toward a ground state. The project asks which logical distinctions survive when the clause set is treated as one physical object at once.

entries.title: spectral-multiplicative-framework
entries.summary: Graph theory meets quantum mechanics in optimization space, implemented in Crystal for a small executable surface. The framework asks which eigenvalues of a constraint graph a decision can afford to forget, and what breaks when the wrong ones are dropped.

entries.title: obs-ai
entries.summary: Obsidian with an AI layer, kept as a knowledge base that can be queried without losing provenance. Notes are indexed so retrieval returns the passage you meant, not the closest wording, and answer can be traced back to its source.

entries.title: banzhaf-ensemble-thesis
entries.summary: Game theory meets ensemble learning through Banzhaf power indices, measuring which features shift a model's vote. The thesis asks how much redundancy an ensemble can carry before the extra members change nothing, and how to tell when they already have.

groups.title: Gists and essays
groups.note: Long-form writing published directly on GitHub, without a repository around it.

entries.title: TATH
entries.summary: A formal treatment of the laboratory's central device, written as a self-contained document. The definitions are tightened until every later project can be checked against them, including which information an abstraction is allowed to discard and what it must keep.

entries.title: How Number Theory Breaks a NP-Hard Problem
entries.summary: An argument that number-theoretic structure can dissolve the apparent hardness of a combinatorial problem rather than merely making it faster. The piece isolates the specific distinction the encoding preserves, and explains why removing that distinction returns the original difficulty unchanged.

entries.title: Computation
entries.summary: An essay on computation as the act of discarding what is irrelevant. It works through what computation must retain, what it may forget, and why two questions are inseparable in every system that has to survive contact with a user.

entries.title: Operator Algebra Blogpost
entries.summary: Operator algebra imported as a language for representation: which parts of a system are interchangeable, and what quotient structure survives that interchange. It is the bridge between physics and the abstraction program, and the clearest statement of the shared vocabulary.

groups.title: Published essays
groups.note: Longer pieces written for the site. They live in the archive repository, held private — write to request access.

entries.title: Fock Space Computation: A Mathematical Framework for Symbolic Information Processing
entries.summary: A formal demonstration that symbolic computation follows quantum field theory mathematics, with experimental validation in parsing and version control. Fock space supplies the state space, and the framework explains why symbolic systems behave like particle systems under construction and annihilation.

entries.title: The Hidden Laws of Imbalance: Advanced Diagnostic Frameworks for Optimization Limits
entries.summary: Diagnostic frameworks for optimisation limits in complex systems, arguing that the right move is often architectural rather than parametric. The essay names the imbalance laws that quietly cap a search, and shows where spending more compute stops helping in practice.

entries.title: Mathematical Mechanism: How the Self-Stabilizing Optimizer Works
entries.summary: Clean, rigorous mathematics behind the exponential-sum manifold and the correlation-based control system applied to NP-hard problems. This is the mechanism write-up: what the solver actually computes, why the correlation term converges, and which guarantees hold for hard instances in practice.

entries.title: A Multiplicative Axis for Constraint Enforcement in Machine Learning
entries.summary: A previously unrecognised axis in loss-design space, built from spectral-multiplicative constraints using analytic number theory and exponential barrier dynamics. The essay shows that constraints can be enforced multiplicatively, preserving properties additive penalties quietly destroy, and explains when this axis helps.

entries.title: The Proximity-Identity Functional: Mathematical Foundations of Equilibrium
entries.summary: A mathematical analysis of the proximity-identity functional and its role in determining equilibrium states across physics, machine learning and information theory. The essay derives the functional's fixed points and shows equilibrium as an identity that survives perturbation of the system.

entries.title: The Hidden Manifold Where Geometry Meets Arithmetic: How We Built a Self-Stabilizing Optimizer
entries.summary: Every optimisation problem, from microchip layouts to cloud allocation, is navigation across an energy landscape. This essay describes the system built to stabilise itself there, replacing brute force with a manifold that contracts toward a solution with no human supervision.

groups.title: Foundations
groups.note: {n} long-form documents on the lab site: the thesis, the axiom geometry, the honest scope, and the bibliography. Read these before the code.

entries.title: The Architecture of Axioms: Geometry, Infinity, and the Prime Code
entries.summary: Axioms are treated as a Boolean lattice whose curvature measures how much each axiom depends on the others. Non-zero curvature is the obstruction to path-independence, and extending the geometry to infinite axiom sets breaks Möbius inversion until primes rescue it.

entries.title: The Arithmetic Manifold
entries.summary: The thesis that constraint satisfaction, optimization and physical simulation are projections of one geometric structure, with five proof points: prime-weighted constraints give every clause a unique fingerprint, so none compete for the same gradient signal and the solver stops stalling.

entries.title: Unified Mathematical Systems Report
entries.summary: A comprehensive assessment of eight shipped solvers and frameworks sharing one mathematical theory, mapping discrete constraints onto continuous energy landscapes with prime weights and multiplicative dynamics. It reports where the speedups are real, and where they are not at all.

entries.title: Papers and Citations
entries.summary: Every publication with a permanent DOI, plus the theoretical foundations they rest on: Kirkpatrick on annealing, Parisi on spin glasses, Corless on Lambert W, and the statistical-physics literature on thresholds. Written for anyone checking the claims rather than admiring them.

entries.title: Related Work
entries.summary: A measured comparison with simulated annealing, quantum annealing, belief propagation, constraint programming and mixed-integer solvers: what each approach assumes, where it overlaps with the spectral-arithmetic line, and where the difference is a genuine difference in kind rather than in engineering.

entries.title: Where Navokoj Works (and Where It Doesn't)
entries.summary: The scope statement, written before the marketing: NitroSAT is an anytime MaxSAT approximator, strong on structured industrial problems and the wrong tool at the phase transition. Benchmarks are reported against certified optima, with the gaps left visible and honestly named.

entries.title: Glossary
entries.summary: A plain-English reference for every term used across the lab's documentation, from BAHA and phase transitions to prime weighting and the partition function. Each entry links to its deeper explanation, so a reader moves from vocabulary into the argument itself.

entries.title: The Design Philosophy
entries.summary: A working document on running five public surfaces and ten shipped projects without flattening them into one template. The rule is simple: tune every surface to what its reader came to do, and let the surfaces disagree where readers differ.

groups.title: Citable records
groups.note: {n} Zenodo records, each the version of record for an artifact. The DOIs are permanent and citable; prefer them over a repository link when you cite.

entries.title: Solving SAT with Quantum Vacuum Dynamics
entries.summary: Partial assignments are treated as physical microstates in an energy landscape, where almost-satisfying configurations attract one another Casimir-style and coagulate into stable solution clusters. The proposal reframes Boolean satisfiability as a physical process, with the implementation and interactive site attached.

entries.title: Spectral-Multiplicative Optimization Framework
entries.summary: An implementation and validation bundle joining heat-kernel spectral theory to number-theoretic constraint encoding, running at O(nnz) on graphs past a hundred thousand nodes while holding spectral action and multiplicative penalties correlated. It ships diagnostics for inherent optimisation limits baked in.

entries.title: ShunyaBar: Spectral-Arithmetic Phase Transitions for Combinatorial Optimization
entries.summary: The umbrella preprint formalising the solver programme as a spectral triple whose partition function factorises over the adelic ring, with KMS states undergoing a phase transition at inverse temperature one. A renormalisation sweep replaces exponential search with a bounded one.

entries.title: Multiplicative Calculus for Hardness Detection and Branch-Aware Optimization
entries.summary: Hardness is located where the log-derivative of a partition function diverges, because the control parameter there lives on a multi-sheeted analytic surface where optimisers fail. A branch-aware optimiser navigates the sheets with Lambert W, cutting complexity from exponential to linear.

entries.title: NitroSAT: A Physics-Informed MaxSAT Solver Using Heat Kernel Diffusion, Persistent Homology, and Branch-Aware Holonomy Annealing
entries.summary: A MaxSAT solver treating constraint satisfaction as a dynamical system on a clause hypergraph, with heat-kernel smoothing, persistent homology for symmetry detection, zeta-guided resonance injection and branch-aware holonomy annealing. It reaches 99.58 percent satisfaction across 358 instances and nineteen families.

entries.title: Emergent Stochasticity from Serialized Concurrency
entries.summary: Uniform randomness is reconstructed as the invariant measure of a deterministic concurrent system forced through a serialising bottleneck, with the interleaving space written as products of symmetric groups. It is a constructive theory of when distinct histories may be pooled.

entries.title: FUTCache — v1.3.0, v1.4.0, v.2.0.0
entries.summary: Adaptive semantic cache calibration, then a visit-set representation that scales to a million production traces. The releases measure the same claim from both directions: how much can be merged away, and how little information may be lost while doing it.

entries.title: NitroSAT — v1.0.0, v3.0.0.0, v3.1.0
entries.summary: A production-ready release, followed by a disk-streaming solver that keeps the working set bounded on instances too large for memory. The streaming design is itself an abstraction: only decision-relevant state survives the write, and nothing else is paid for anyway.

entries.title: NoetherLeap — v1.0
entries.summary: The first stable release of constraint-aware optimization, pairing physics-informed networks with Bayesian search and symmetry discovery. Conserved quantities prune the search space without removing any reachable optimum, and the symmetries are reported rather than simply assumed to hold in advance.

entries.title: reify — v0.1.0, v0.2.0
entries.summary: Initial release and first refinement of a declarative SDK for constraint optimization, hosted under the ShunyaBar Labs organisation. Constraints are declared once and the compiler decides what can be safely removed, which is the whole research program in miniature form.

groups.title: Podcast — Space Time Cafe
groups.note: {n} entries — the lab's argument in spoken form: one long-form video essay per topic, plus the playlist overview.

entries.title: Space Time Cafe
entries.summary: A long-form video essay series in which physics, number theory, geometry and machine learning are argued through together. Fifty-one episodes published between February 2025 and August 2026 range over primes, infinity, chaos, operators, fairness and the limits of computation itself.

entries.title: Episode 1 : The Lore Behind Majorana Quantum Chip
entries.summary: The series opens on Ettore Majorana, who vanished in 1938, and the fermions that carry his name. The episode reconstructs the story, explains what makes them neutral and self-conjugate, and traces how a particle became a candidate for quantum hardware.

entries.title: Episode 2 : The Majorana-Riemann Hypothesis Connection – A Breakdown
entries.summary: The second episode presses the link between Majorana fermions and the Riemann hypothesis, working through how topological superconductivity encodes prime behaviour, where the analogy holds, and where the mathematics is doing real work rather than merely sounding deep and impressive.

entries.title: Episode 3: Unraveling Infinity’s Code
entries.summary: Einstein's continuous infinity against Wolfram's computational treatment of the infinite, with the argument that infinity is a constraint of description rather than a thing that exists. The episode asks what changes if the universe is explored algorithmically instead of analytically.

entries.title: Episode 6: The Monster Problem: Fibonacci’s Deepest Secrets (Part 2)
entries.summary: Part two of the Fibonacci sequence: whether primes hide a code when written in Fibonacci base, and what that means for finding them. The episode works through the monster problem and asks whether arithmetic structure could resolve an open question.

entries.title: Episode 4: Computational Infinity: The Universe's Hidden Code
entries.summary: What if infinity is not real, and every infinite is a computational limit not yet reached. The episode develops computational infinity as a working alternative to continuous analysis, and tests it against the places classical mathematics refuses to ever terminate.

entries.title: Episode 5: Fibonacci Unraveled: The Math, the Mystery, and the Magic (Part 1)
entries.summary: Part one: the Fibonacci sequence from first principles, its closed form, and the golden ratio it converges to, then outward to sunflowers, spirals and galaxies. The episode asks why one recurrence appears everywhere it does, and what it is counting.

entries.title: Episode 7: Fibonacci’s Hidden Duality: Growth vs Decay
entries.summary: The same recurrence, with initial conditions nudged, produces decay instead of growth. The episode explores eigenmode cancellation in detail and the parameter at which exponential growth flips sign, treating the pair of behaviours as one object seen from two sides.

entries.title: Episode 8: Primes, Chaos, and the Quantum Code | Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Primes mimic quantum randomness using arithmetic alone: the episode works through chaotic maps over the primes, their spectral behaviour, and why the pattern is indistinguishable from quantum while being entirely classical in origin, then asks what would separate the explanations.

entries.title: Episode 9: Prime Chaos and the Secret p-adic Vortex of Randomness - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Prime vortex maps, the swirling flows of quantum materials, and the p-adic number line placed side by side, arguing that randomness at different scales has one single structure, and that the vortex is where number theory becomes fluid and computable.

entries.title: Episode 10: Patterns in Primes: Structure, Entropy, and the Nature of Intelligence - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Structure, entropy and the nature of intelligence drawn together through the primes: the episode asks whether the irregularity of the primes carries information, and whether a system that could read that irregularity would count as intelligent in any meaningful sense.

entries.title: Episode 11: The Beauty and Power of Invariants - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Invariants as the hidden order beneath mathematics, using the fraction matrix problem to show how the smallest fractions behave and why quantities that survive every transformation are the ones worth tracking. The episode asks what an invariant is really for.

entries.title: Episode 12: The Terminal Algebra of the Event Horizon - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Zero point algebra, the algebraic structure at the boundary where nothing returns, and what it says about descriptions of the impossible. The episode works through the system, its operations, and the limits of the framework itself, and where it stops.

entries.title: Episode 13:  Concurrency Invariant and the Singularity - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Cloud workflows, collapse of consciousness, classical and quantum computing, all unified by one claimed law: that concurrency has an invariant. The episode states the law, argues it from several directions, and asks what it would predict if it were true.

entries.title: Episode 14: Ghosts, Eternal Inflation, and the Boundaries of Singularity Algebra - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Two of Hawking's papers, living with ghosts and the final boundary of the universe, read as a stress test for singularity algebra. The episode asks whether the algebra can account for what the physics actually says, and where it stops.

entries.title: Encrypting with Chaos:- ChaosEncrypt - Episode 12 - Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: ChaosEncrypt, a cipher built on deterministic chaotic maps, with prime-driven keystreams and HMAC key exchange. The episode walks through the construction, explains why chaotic systems resist prediction, and is about the difference between a research tool and a production cipher.

entries.title: Episode 13: The Hidden Geometry of Language Models and Thought | Spacetime Cafe
entries.summary: Counting, arithmetic and primes connected through Riemannian geometry and singularities, with large language models as the test case. The episode asks whether the geometry of a model's internal representations is recoverable at all, and what counting means in that space.

entries.title: Episode 14: The Strange Reality of Fractals and Hyperbolic Space  | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Fractional dimensions and hyperbolic geometry through the idea of precision dimension: how a measure can sit between integers, and what the hyperbolic space does to notions of distance, scale and self-similarity that Euclidean intuition cannot reach or even represent well.

entries.title: Episode 15: Visualizing the Cantor Set in Hyperbolic Space | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The Cantor set remade in hyperbolic space, where chopping an interval behaves quite differently than it does in the line. The episode is part proof, part visualisation, showing how the classical construction changes and what survives the change of geometry.

entries.title: Episode 16: How Prime Numbers Shape Geometry | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The Dynamic Prime Cantor set, the fat variant, and the structures primes generate when they are allowed to determine the geometry. The episode follows the construction and asks what it means for arithmetic to be the thing carving the space.

entries.title: Episode 17: From Prime Fractals to Multiverse Islands | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Prime fractals read against inverted islands, entanglement and branching cosmologies alike. The episode draws the parallel honestly and precisely: where the analogy is structural rather than decorative, and where the multiverse framing is doing philosophical rather than purely mathematical work.

entries.title: Episode 18: The Mathematical Tug of War between Identity and Proximity |  SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: A balance between similarity and difference, appearing in machine learning, quantum physics and perception all at once. The episode builds the tension formally and asks when two things should be treated as the same, and when they must not be.

entries.title: Episode 19: Dynamic Choice and the Geometry of Now | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The present as a saddle point where a Euclidean past meets a fractal future, and the account of choice and time that follows. The episode develops geometry, then asks what freedom looks like when the now is a fixed point.

entries.title: Ep  20 Trailer:  Regularizing Divergence with Convergence  | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: A short trailer: collapsing divergent sequences rather than discarding them, and the core insight behind regularizing divergence with convergence. It is a ninety-second door into the argument that non-convergence can be handled by changing what the limit is taken over.

entries.title: Episode 20: Spectral Symmetry Confinement Principle | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Symmetry as the hidden force shaping both quantum particles and the primes, stated as the Spectral Symmetry Confinement Principle. The episode formulates the principle, gives it consequences, and asks whether it is a law or a pattern, or a coincidence.

entries.title: Episode 21: Primefall: The Precision Descent | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: A game of number theory, chaos and high stakes: Prime Fall, where a descent through precision replaces the game mechanics. The episode plays it, reads the mathematics inside the rules, and asks what the design teaches about exploration and play.

entries.title: Episode 22: The Physics of Story Telling | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Reality as a language with physics as its grammar: how quantum mechanics, emotion and narrative form interact in a single account. The episode argues that storytelling is a physical process, and that the mechanism is measurable rather than merely metaphorical.

entries.title: Episode 23: Mystery of Self-Adjoint Operators | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Wigner's puzzle about the unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics, approached through self-adjoint operators and the conditions under which an operator is genuinely observable. The episode works through the spectral theorem and asks why physics keeps choosing structures that work so well.

entries.title: Episode 24 : Operator Theory of Everything -  SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Five codes, one cosmos: a framework blending operator theory with philosophy, and the mathematics carried rather than gestured at. The episode argues that the same operator language describes physics, computation and mind, and asks what it would take to refute.

entries.title: Episode 25: Artificial Substrate Intelligence | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Intelligence that emerges from the substrate rather than the model, moving from philosophical argument to engineering. The episode asks what changes when intelligence is a property of the arrangement of matter rather than of a program trained on text alone.

entries.title: Episode 26: The Thermodynamics of Purpose | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: What it means for something to have purpose, worked through thermodynamics and information theory rather than ethics. The episode asks whether agency can be defined by energy accounting alone, and what a purpose-free system looks like in practice to us.

entries.title: Episode 27: The Shape of Unsolvable Problems | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Obstruction theory and why certain problems feel unsolvable: the gerbe twist and what it implies across mathematics, physics and computation. The episode argues that unsolvability has a shape, and that seeing that shape deliberately changes what you try next time.

entries.title: Episode 27 Trailer | Fiber Bundles and Gerbes | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: A short trailer for the gerbe episode, introducing fiber bundles and gerbes as the hidden architecture of inconsistency, and previewing the argument that some contradictions are structural rather than accidental, and not simply a failure of effort, attention or nerve.

entries.title: Episode 28: Why Hard Problems Bend Reality | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The curved geometry of problem spaces, argued through Sudoku and ordinary decisions, and what curvature does to strategy. The episode shows that hard problems are not merely harder but differently shaped, and that the shape should guide the method chosen.

entries.title: Episode 29: Geometry of Chaos and Order | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Prime numbers against reverse gerbes, and the geometry of chaos and order built from them. The episode works through how order emerges inside apparent randomness, and what the reverse construction makes visible that the forward one hides at first glance.

entries.title: Episode 30: Mathematics with a Pulse | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Spectral logic: proofs treated as thermodynamic journeys with energy bills, prime-weighted costs assigned to each step. The episode argues that mathematics can be made to pay for itself, and asks what a cost function for proof would buy in practice.

entries.title: Episode 31: The Physics of Thought | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Creativity through cognitive thermodynamics, examining intelligence through thermodynamics and harmonic analysis. The episode asks whether thinking is a physical process with constraints, and whether those constraints are informative rather than merely limiting, and whether creativity means escaping them at all.

entries.title: Are we in a Simulation? | Explainer Video
entries.summary: A short explainer on whether the world is a simulation, approached with scientific tools rather than speculation. It lays out what each hypothesis would predict, what evidence would distinguish them, and why the question is harder than it first appears.

entries.title: Episode 32: Ramanujan Graphs | Elegant Networks for a Complex World | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Ramanujan's intuition and the graphs that carry it forward: networks with strong spectral properties, used in modern communications and codes. The episode traces the story from a self-taught genius to a deployed technology, and asks what else he saw coming.

entries.title: Episode 33: The Rhythm of Encryption | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Keys that are not stored data but the evolving rhythm of a living system. The episode develops the idea, asks what it buys against an adversary, and is frank about how much of it is proposal rather than deployed practice.

entries.title: Episode 34: General Relativity of Information | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Whether reality is fixed or partly constructed by observation, through spectral redundancy and a proposed unified theory of complex systems. The episode develops the claim and asks what would count as evidence against it, and whether any such could exist.

entries.title: Episode 35: What Makes Something Real? | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Inspired by an eight-year-old's question, matter versus mind versus resources, and what makes something real at all. The episode takes the question seriously, works through the philosophical positions, and ends with something closer to a method than to an answer.

entries.title: Episode 36: Speed Limit of Intelligence | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The claim that intelligence has a fundamental speed limit, argued from neuroscience, complex systems and physics. The episode asks what such a limit would be made of, whether it could be evaded, and how you would notice it in practice.

entries.title: Podcast Introduction
entries.summary: A fourteen-second bumper introducing the podcast, and a reminder of what the series is for: long conversations about the places where physics, mathematics and computation meet, and a first taste of the argument that runs through all forty of them.

entries.title: Episode 37:  Splitting the Unsplittable  | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Fair division in computer science: partitioning data so that no party is systematically worse off, and the approximation guarantees that make it tractable. The episode works through the cake-cutting line of results and asks what fairness costs computationally, and when.

entries.title: Episode 38: The Circle that helps Intelligence | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Seven points on a circle, and from them a synthesis bridging geometry, number theory and artificial intelligence alike. The episode builds the construction stepwise, then asks whether the circle helps machines think or only helps us describe how they do.

entries.title: Episode 39: The Shape of Fairness | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: What fairness means for a system, a market or a society, challenging the usual definitions in favour of a geometric account. The episode asks what shape fairness has, and whether it can be measured without reducing it to a scalar.

entries.title: Episode 40: The Perfect Arithmetic Resistor | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: Anti-superconductors and non-commutative geometry, with the hidden quantum order of the primes. The episode walks through the prime-annealer paper and blog at length, and asks whether arithmetic can insulate a material the way geometry insulates an ordinary semiconductor device today.

entries.title: Episode 41: Prime Walk | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The prime walk, a number-line puzzle, taken seriously as a route into symmetry breaking and the Riemann hypothesis. The episode follows the walk, the Jahn-Teller analogy, and the specific sense in which primes behave like quantum particles in the laboratory.

entries.title: Episode 42: The Geometry of Knowledge | SpaceTime Cafe
entries.summary: The geometry underpinning mathematical understanding, taken from the Floer hardness certificates paper. The episode asks whether knowledge has structure that can be measured, what persistent homology contributes to the question, and whether a certificate is the right thing to want.

entries.title: The Physics of Divergent Computation
entries.summary: What an infinite loop is really tracing: divergent computation as a hidden mathematical structure rather than a plain failure. The episode connects frozen loading screens to the mathematics of divergence, and asks what it would mean to wait correctly, eventually.

entries.title: Gravity Is Just Biased Attention: The Math Connecting Physics and AI
entries.summary: The claim that asymmetric attention in physics and hallucination in transformers share one piece of mathematics. The episode works through the column-imbalance result and asks what a link between gravity and attention would have to explain, and whether it survives.

groups.title: Elsewhere
groups.note: {n} other doors into the lab: the front door, the notebook, the shipping API, the browser build, the community, the theory portal and the evidence ledger.

entries.title: Research notebook
entries.summary: The lab notebook: essays sorted into tribes covering core theory, number theory, optimization, with a mindmap of how the projects compose. It is the early face of the work, and says that the entries are exploratory rather than finished proofs.

entries.title: Navokoj
entries.summary: The production solver API behind the lab's work: Navokoj serves MaxSAT over plain HTTP, with proof artifacts you can verify offline and an anytime guarantee that returns the best assignment found. It is the shipping version of the research line.

entries.title: Evidence ledger
entries.summary: A ledger of evidence artifacts: benchmark runs, results and numbers quoted in the papers. It exists so claims can be checked against the runs that produced them, and each figure has somewhere to be traced back to its own source.

entries.title: Lab homepage
entries.summary: The lab's front door: one page stating the thesis, the numbers behind it, and the routes into the solver, the API and the notebook. The shortest path for a visitor who has never heard of the lab and wants more.

entries.title: BAHA beta app
entries.summary: The browser build of the escape mechanism, running the solver in the cloud and showing the branch-aware trajectory as it happens. It is the quickest way to watch the theory work on an instance you care about, without installing anything.

entries.title: SBL community
entries.summary: The community around the lab: a Discord with people working on solvers, constraint systems and the deeper mathematics underneath them. Open questions get posted daily, results get argued about, and the people behind the papers sit in the channel there.

entries.title: Theory portal
entries.summary: The formal architecture of the spectral-arithmetic system, still being written: the axioms, the geometry, the quotient structure and the open questions. It is the deepest door into the lab, and it is currently a placeholder while the proofs are settled.
